static_traits.name: Chen Tao
static_traits.family_status: Grew up in a family with 6 siblings, parents Divorced; currently a Widower
static_traits.social_status: Sociable, able to maintain Interpersonal relationships, but has not yet fully opened up to others about deep Guilt and self-blame
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness;not yet received relevant psychological counseling/treatment in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic; initially rather tense, not used to opening up; able to unfold gradually with Guidance, willing to try new perspectives; calm tone

basic_info.main_problem: I have been in pain and guilt over my parents' Divorce; I believe I may be the cause of their Divorce, thus feeling continuous self-blame and sadness; these feelings intensified after being Widowed, affecting daily life and sleep.
basic_info.core_demands: I do not want to keep feeling this way.
growth_experiences: Parents divorced in childhood: he grew up in a large family with 6 siblings; his parents, long under financial pressure and affected by the father's long working hours, often quarreled. The client remembers that once, after he argued with his mother over a trivial matter, his parents immediately erupted into a fierce quarrel and his father left home. This situation made him strongly connect his parents' divorce with his own behavior, forming long-lasting self-blame and the belief 'It was all caused by me'.

Spouse's death in adulthood: after becoming a Widower, old trauma and guilt about parents' Divorce were strongly activated; the client began attributing the spouse's Death to themselves as well, thinking 'I must have done something wrong'; sadness and self-blame significantly intensified, affecting sleep and daily functioning.

core_beliefs: All bad things It is all my fault
I am a person who disappoints others and annoys people

special_situations.event: In childhood, after an argument with Mother, parents immediately had a big fight and Father left home
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I behave improperly or talk back, it will trigger serious consequences, even breaking the family apart
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to be a 'good child', blaming problems on oneself to maintain order and a sense of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault; they divorced because of me

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others can maintain happy families but I cannot, it means I am a failure and something is wrong with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids related scenes, distracting attention through busy work and socializing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They can all manage their families well, but I let my own family fall apart; I did something wrong

special_situations.event: Recalls memories of parents arguing more easily when they were present
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they argue more when I am present, it means I am the trigger and they do not like me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing expression of true needs, being cautious in words and actions, avoiding 'causing trouble'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I annoy them; they argue because of me

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If unfortunate events happen, they must be related to me; only by taking responsibility and reflecting on myself can I avoid losing again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly blames himself, agonizing over 'what I did wrong' to gain a sense of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I had done better then, he would not have passed away; It is all my fault

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and cared for by parents/significant others, maintaining relationship stability and completeness
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being abandoned, blamed, and losing important others (relationship rupture/Death)
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control over the relationship through self-blame and over-responsibility, reducing the fear of abandonment
Repressing disappointment and anger toward others to avoid triggering further conflict or loss

object_relations.self_representation: A child/partner who is at fault and will ruin the family
object_relations.object_representation: Parents who are easily hurt and would leave because of oneself

object_relations.self_representation: Bears responsibility for the loss, a person who needs self-examination
object_relations.object_representation: A significant other who is vulnerable and might be harmed by him or leave (such as a spouse)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes 'you may not be the only reason for your parents' divorce' or tries to reduce their self-blame
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I do not take the blame upon myself, it equals letting myself off the hook, which is undeserved
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in a self-blaming tone, repeatedly emphasizing 'It is all my fault', downplaying other causes; reducing emotional expression, restrained tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to review evidence and consider other factors such as money pressure and the father's long working hours
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing the counselor is downplaying one's responsibility, and that only emphasizing one's own fault is honest
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses causal inference and concrete examples to prove 'it is my fault', with a calm tone but holding firmly to their view, repeating personalized attribution.

manifestations: The Widowed event triggering intense grief and self-blame, attributing the spouse's Death to one's own 'having done something wrong'
When seeing happy families or couples, the pain and guilt about loss significantly intensify
outcomes: Trying to gain a sense of control through self-blame

manifestations: Self-describing as 'sociable but not yet truly open', deep Guilt and self-blame not yet fully expressed to others
Not used to opening up about these feelings, initially rather tense
outcomes: Access to emotional support is limited; inner burdens accumulate over the long term
Replacing deep processing of emotions with distraction; symptoms persist

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Believing 'should not let oneself off the hook', maintaining harsh standards toward oneself
Expressing cautiously in counseling, worrying that 'letting oneself off' is undeserved

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizing the rule 'I must be good and not cause trouble'
Uses 'should/must' to demand self take on more responsibility

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not expressing disappointment and anger about parents' relationship, turning instead to self-blame and being harsh on oneself
More often choosing self-Repression and distraction when emotions run high

positive_force: Strong sociability, with a certain support network (friends to talk to)
Willing to seek help and express the wish 'to change', can cooperate with reality testing
Able to identify other causes in relationships (like financial pressure, Father Working long hours), with some cognitive flexibility
negative_force: Deep-rooted personalization and overgeneralization thinking, persistent self-blame
Strongly triggering guilt and sadness when seeing happy families/couples or recalling parents' arguments
Relying on distraction rather than processing emotions; deep feelings hard to express

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-blame and attributing negative events to himself (personalized attribution)
antecedent: Asked by others or self-reflecting on the reasons for the family breakdown
target_behavior.core_reason: In childhood, linked parents' quarrels with their own behavior and internalized the belief 'When something goes wrong it is my fault', forming cognitive biases of personalization and overgeneralization.
target_behavior.function: Gaining a superficial sense of control, avoiding facing disappointment and powerlessness toward parents, while trying to prevent losing again through self-blame.
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent guilt and sadness, Sleep affected, impaired daily functioning and physical and mental health.

target_behavior.behavior: Uses busyness and socializing to disperse emotions (avoidant distraction)
antecedent: When cues related to family/loss appear
target_behavior.core_reason: Reduces suffering in the short term; avoids the need to directly face traumatic memories and strong emotions.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome emotional experiences, temporarily relieving emotional pressure.
target_behavior.consequence: Emotions not yet fully processed, problems recurring and maintained.
